name: Diffuse Idiopathic Skeletal Hyperostosis

criteria.description: Flowing calcification and ossification along the anterolateral aspect of at least four contiguous vertebral bodies
Preservation of intervertebral disc height without significant degenerative changes
Absence of apophyseal joint ankylosis and sacroiliac joint erosion or fusion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of flowing ossification along at least four contiguous vertebrae with preserved disc height and absence of apophyseal or sacroiliac joint involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiological; clinical symptoms may be mild or absent.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Flowing ossification along anterolateral vertebral bodies

occasional.symptomName: Peripheral enthesopathy (e.g., at Achilles tendon insertion)

rare.symptomName: Airway obstruction due to large cervical osteophytes

imaging: X-ray showing flowing ossification along anterolateral vertebral bodies
CT scan demonstrating ligamentous calcification and ossification
MRI to assess spinal cord or nerve root compression
genetic: No known genetic mutations definitively linked
other: Histopathology shows ossification of entheses and ligaments

distinguishingFeatures: Sacroiliac joint involvement with erosion and fusion
Disc space narrowing and osteophyte formation without flowing ossification
Ossification localized to posterior longitudinal ligament

references: Resnick D, Niwayama G. Radiographic and pathologic features of spinal involvement in diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH). Radiology. 1976.
Mader R, Verlaan JJ, Buskila D. Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis: clinical features and pathogenic mechanisms. Nat Rev Rheumatol. 2013.
Kuperus JS, et al. Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis: a systematic review of epidemiology and clinical characteristics. Semin Arthritis Rheum. 2019.
